Subject: BlueWhale session-shape declaration & preflight sizing

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To speed the Dedicated proposal (and make sure we size the GPU mix correctly), can you complete the short session-shape declaration below and attach a small sample of traffic (CSV or JSON) if available? You can find our starter worksheet attached — filling the shaded rows is sufficient.

Key asks (short):
- Typical requests per minute (avg and peak 95th)
- Prompt length and average generated token length (median and 95th)
- Session behavior: ephemeral single-turn vs multi-turn (avg turns per session)
- Concurrency target / P99 latency SLO for interactive paths
- Percent of requests that need high-quality decoding (slow) vs fast decoding (cheap)

If easier, paste the answers inline and I’ll convert them into our sizing model. Target timeline: get this back by EOD Thu so we can include numbers in the pilot SOW.

Attachments: bluewhale_preflight_sizing.xlsx (worksheet)

Thanks —
Grace

Hi Grace —

Apologies for the slow reply — attached is a small dump of anonymized traffic (bluewhale_traffic_sample.csv) and our answers below. Let me know if you want the raw event schema.

Answers (short):
- Typical requests per minute (avg): 120 rpm; peak 95th: 1,100 rpm (short flash sales)
- Prompt length: median 45 tokens; 95th 320 tokens
- Generated length: median 60 tokens; 95th 980 tokens (long summary mode)
- Session behavior: mix — 70% single-turn, 30% multi-turn; avg turns per multi-turn session: 6
- Concurrency target: 450 concurrent sessions sustained for peak window; P99 latency SLO: 500 ms for interactive endpoints
- High-quality decode %: 18% of requests flagged for high-quality (nucleus sampling with larger beam)
- Average context (prefix) reuse: 40% of requests hit similar prefixes (we do caching client-side sometimes)
- Typical model: open-variant (we're flexible) but we expect to require fp16/4-bit quantized variants in production

Notes: peak windows are usually 20–30 minutes during promotional pushes; typical burst shape is sharp with ~5–8x baseline. We redacted user ids in the CSV.

Thanks —
Lena Park
Head of Platform Engineering, BlueWhale AI
lena@bluewhale.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: BlueWhale session-shape declaration & preflight sizing

Forwarding Lena's answers — quick read and thoughts below.

Summary: 120 rpm baseline, 1,100 rpm 95th, median in/out tokens low but 95th generated tokens ~980 — so we have a long-tail. 30% multi-turn with avg 6 turns — KV-cache useful. 18% high-quality. Peak bursts 5–8x for 20–30 mins.

My immediate sizing notes (ballpark):
- For interactive endpoints with 500 ms P99 and 450 sustained concurrency, we should plan for ~8–10 A100/4090-class nodes in reserved pool if we run a higher-capacity quantized model; higher if the model is larger. But the long 95th outputs push token costs and may require GPU memory headroom for KV cache (multi-turn).
- Suggest split-routing: canary 20% to high-quality CCD (larger model on beefier nodes), 80% to quantized lower-latency variant. That aligns with 18% HQ traffic.
- Need to understand session average sequence length for batching assumptions — the CSV sample will help.

Questions for Grace / Karthik:
1) Can we identify the model family they're expecting to run? (open-variant name or token budget)
2) Should we propose autoscale burst pools for the 20–30 minute spikes, or reserve additional burst quota?
3) Any compliance/pinning needs for BlueWhale re: private deployment? (Lena CC'd procurement)

I can draft a quick GPU mix slide once we confirm model family.

-Marissa

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.inference>
To: Lena Park <lena@bluewhale.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueWhale session-shape declaration & preflight sizing

Thanks Lena — this is great context and the sample looks clean. Quick clarifications and proposal: 

Clarifications (so our sizing has fewer assumptions):
- Can you confirm the 980-token outputs are deterministic summarization workloads (single request per user) vs iterative streaming completion? If streaming, we need to budget more for throughput.
- For the 30% multi-turn traffic, is the 6-turn average including short metadata-only heartbeats or full prompt exchanges? That affects KV cache size.

Prelim proposal (we'll formalize in the SOW):
- Reserved pool: 6 × H100-equivalent nodes for the quantized production variant (handles baseline + most of burst via autoscaling headroom).
- Burst/overflow: 2 × H100-equivalent prewarmed nodes in a transient burst pool to cover the 5–8x 20–30m spikes (automated routing into overflow).
- High-quality lane: 2 × A100/80GB-class nodes for the 18% HQ traffic or run HQ on the same fleet with priority scheduling — we'll include cost trade-offs in the proposal.
- Caching: recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for 30% multi-turn traffic and an LRU size tuned to median 45-token prefixes (we'll recommend a default and we can tune in pilot).

Next steps:
- Lena: confirm the two clarifications above + whether BlueWhale prefers reserved burst quota (monthly commit) vs on-demand autoscale for overflow.
- Marissa / Karthik / Camila: I'll hand off the CSV to the sizing model and draft the GPU mix slides + rough cost run-rate. Marissa — can you own the draft SOW?

Grace
